text:
Kirill Marchenko came off injured reserve on Friday, back after a month out (his last game before this was a seven-minute night in Calgary on Oct. 26), and the headlines all week framed his return as the jolt the slumping Leafs needed. He played 15 and a half minutes in a 3-1 win in Boston, no points, one shot. Fine for a first game back.

Before the injury he was exactly what Toronto hoped for in his first season there: 14 points in 15 games, 8 on the power play, and a 56% share of the 5v5 expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, nearly 11 points better than the team without him.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains the scoring: he gets to the home-plate area in front of the net (90th percentile among forwards last season) and gets the best passes. The thing to watch is his minutes. If they climb back toward 17 to 18 a night, the Leafs have their scorer back.
